Usage

Geodesic distances from source to all points (Dijkstra on a kNN graph). → (N,) float (unreachable points are inf).

Makes the k-nearest-neighbour graph built by knn_graph(points, k) (edge weight = Euclidean distance between points = chord length) undirected with directed=False and solves the single-source shortest paths with scipy.sparse.csgraph.dijkstra. d[i] is the path length on the graph from source to point i, with d[source] = 0; points in connected components not connected to source are inf. Units are the coordinate units unchanged.

• points: (N,3) point cloud (converted to float64).

• source: index of the start point (an integer in 0..N-1; out of range raises an exception on the scipy side).

• k: number of neighbours (default 8). Small values fragment the graph and increase inf; large values create "shortcuts" directly joining distant surfaces, giving distances that do not follow the surface (front and back of a thin plate, folded surfaces, etc.).

Accuracy: since edges are chords, arcs are slightly underestimated, while zigzag in the path causes overestimation (see the sandwich bound of Bernstein et al. in the module docstring). If a triangle mesh is available, use geodesic_mesh, which does not depend on the number of neighbours. For even subsampling by this distance, use farthest_point_sampling.

The 3d op geodesic_distances bridged into the 2-D evolution registry. The implementation is the same; only the calling convention is adapted to op(v, a, b). a sweeps k (default 8). b is unused.
